evidence.excerpt: A Kremlin-affiliated milblogger claimed that the Russian Dnepr GoF recently advanced in Mala Tokmachka (southeast of Orikhiv), that this advance will enable Russian infiltrations toward Preobrezhenka (just north of Orikhiv), and that the Russian Eastern GoF is supporting these efforts by outflanking Ukrainian forces near Chervona Krynytsya (southwest of Hulyaipole and northeast of Orikhiv). The two GoFs are likely attempting to converge on Ukrainian forces from the western and eastern flanks to seize Orikhiv and subsequently push toward Zaporizhzhia City from the southeast.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War (ISW)
evidence.excerpt: Russian forces additionally infiltrated into southern Preobrazhenka (immediately north of Orikhiv), central Mala Tokmachka, and northern Chervona Krynytsia (northeast of Orikhiv), according to geolocated footage published on September 12 and 13. Mashovets indicated that Russian forces made these tactically significant gains in the Orikhiv direction prior to September 1 but stated that Russian forces have since failed to exploit these gains.

evidence.publisher: ArmyInform (Ukrainian Ministry of Defense news agency)
evidence.excerpt: The head of communications of Ukraine's 154th Mechanized Brigade, Orest Drymalovskyi, said Russian assaults in the Hulyaipole direction had decreased from 20–30 per day to about 10 because of losses. He said Russian troops conducted assaults on foot in groups of two or three soldiers, sometimes individually, seeking to infiltrate between Ukrainian positions and accumulate in areas they could reach.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War (ISW)
evidence.excerpt: A Russian milblogger claimed on September 11 that Russian forces are attempting to encircle and assault Orikhiv. The milblogger claimed that elements of the Russian Dnepr Grouping of Forces shifted their assaults towards Preobrazhenka (just northeast of Orikhiv) and secured positions near Novopavlivka (northwest of Orikhiv) and Mala Tokmachka (southeast of Orikhiv) as part of Russia’s encirclement efforts. Another Russian milblogger claimed that Ukrainian fortifications are impeding Russian offensive operations east and southeast of Orikhiv.

question: US reissues Iran oil sanction relief by August 31?
rules:
On July 7, 2026, the United States revoked a sanctions waiver, “General License X,” which allowed for the sale of Iranian oil (see: https://thehill.com/policy/energy-environment/5957647-iran-oil-sanctions-waiver-strait-of-hormuz/).

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States federal government issues a waiver, license, or equivalent sanctions-relief mechanism lifting US sanctions on the sale of Iranian oil, petrochemical products, or petroleum products by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to “No”.

Actions which direct partial or full sanction relief will both qualify. However, qualifying actions must reverse, remove, waive, or suspend US penalties on the sale of Iranian oil, petrochemical products, or petroleum products, in whole or in part.

Qualifying actions need not be permanent; temporary suspensions of sanctions will qualify. Relief issued for either primary or secondary sanctions will qualify. A re-issuance of the initial waiver will qualify. The full removal of any sanction on the sale of Iranian oil, petrochemical products, or petroleum products will also qualify.

Iran's top negotiator said reopening the Strait of Hormuz required the United States to lift its blockade of Iranian ports, lift oil sanctions, release frozen assets, and end threats and military operations on all fronts. Except for necessary wind-down activity, it did not authorize new transactions, including purchases or loading of Iranian-origin products on or after July 7.

question: Will the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia (LDPR) win the second-most seats in the next Russian parliamentary election?
rules:
Parliamentary elections are scheduled to be held in Russia in September 2026.

This market will resolve according to the political party that wins the second greatest number of seats in the next Russian State Duma election.

If the results are not known definitively by September 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The named parties or coalitions will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more parties are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If parties remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed party abbreviations. This market will resolve to the party that occupies the second finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party in the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation.

This market will resolve based on the results of this election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results reported by Russian governm

evidence.excerpt: VCIOM's September 4 release reported party support of 37.2% for United Russia, 11.6% for the Communist Party (CPRF), 11.5% for New People, 8.7% for LDPR and 5.3% for A Just Russia. The survey covered August 24–30, 2026, with 1,600 adult respondents, a combined telephone and household-interview sample, and a stated maximum sampling error of 2.5%.

Vedomosti reported that FOM's August 28–30 survey put United Russia at 33%, LDPR at 11%, CPRF at 9%, New People at 4% and A Just Russia at 3%. LDPR's support increased four percentage points from the preceding survey. FOM interviewed 1,500 respondents in 97 settlements across 51 Russian regions.

Vedomosti reported that FOM's August 21–23 survey placed CPRF at 10%, LDPR at 7% and New People at 6%, while VCIOM's August 17–23 survey placed them at 11.7%, 9.7% and 10.8%, respectively. Political analyst Ilya Grashchenkov said differences between these parties were within the surveys' statistical margins and that several weeks of sustained movement mattered more than weekly fluctuations. He described CPRF as relying on a disciplined protest electorate, LDPR as trying to preserve Zhirinovsky's legacy, and New People as having growth potential among younger and urban voters.

question: Will Elaine Pelino win the 2026 Rhode Island Governor Republican primary election?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the Republican Primary for Governor of Rhode Island, scheduled to take place on September 8, 2026. Resolution will be based on the overall winner of the primary, including any potential second round or run-off.

If no 2026 Rhode Island Gubernatorial Republican Primary takes place, this market will resolve to “Other.”

The resolution source for this market will be the first official announcement of the results from the Rhode Island Republican Party; however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

evidence.excerpt: Among Republican primary voters, Elaine Pelino (37%) has a 20-percentage point lead over Aaron Guckian (17%) heading into the GOP primary for governor, while a whopping 44% of likely Republican primary voters reported they were still undecided. The survey was directed by Pell Center Associate Director and Fellow Katie Sonder and fielded by Embold Research between August 3-11, 2026. It surveyed 857 likely 2026 primary voters in Rhode Island with a margin of error of 3.6%.

Guckian, 50, a former aide to Gov. Don Carcieri who also ran for lieutenant governor in 2022, launched his 2026 campaign as a “compassionate conservative” focused on affordability and government efficiency. Pelino, 72, a first-time candidate, proudly proclaims herself as the “only MAGA candidate” in the primary, promising to keep the left-leaning state from continuing down a path toward “socialism.” The two GOP rivals also espoused similar conservative talking points about increasing government efficiency and accountability while reducing state spending and taxes.

For the quarter ending June 30, Aaron Guckian reported $9,088.49 in donations, $61,011.55 in spending and $30,190.38 in cash on hand. Elaine Pelino reported $2,124.99 in donations, $2,022.68 in spending and $3,142.95 in cash on hand. Second-quarter campaign finance reports were due to the Rhode Island Board of Elections by 11:59 p.m. on July 31.

The survey also took the pulse of 145 Republican primary voters in a three-way gubernatorial contest between Aaron Guckian, Elaine Pelino and Robert Raimondo, though Raimondo has since withdrawn. Pelino, a former comedian and first-time candidate, was backed by more than four in 10 primary voters, while Guckian, the state GOP’s endorsed candidate, received 17% support. Another four in 10 Republican primary voters were undecided, according to the survey. The margin of error for questions specific to Republican primary voters was 8.1%.

Guckian secured the Republican endorsement over primary rival Elaine Pelino by a 72-44 vote, with 10 participants opting not to endorse, according to information supplied by William Ricci Jr., secretary for the state party convention. Endorsements were made by secret ballot. Party-endorsed candidates get top placement on primary ballots.

question: Will the Fed Pause–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Jun–Jul–Sep)?
rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds rate. The decisions on the target federal funds rate are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: June 16-17; July 28-29; and September 15-16.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/f

evidence.excerpt: Both nonfarm payroll employment (-23,000) and the unemployment rate (4.1 percent) changed little in July, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. The change in total nonfarm payroll employment for May was revised down by 66,000, from +129,000 to +63,000, and the change for June was revised down by 37,000, from +57,000 to +20,000. With these revisions, employment in May and June combined is 103,000 lower than previously reported.

The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.1 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in July after falling 0.4 percent in June, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. The all items index rose 3.4 percent for the 12 months ending July after rising 3.5 percent for the 12 months ending June. The all items less food and energy index rose 2.5 percent over the year, following a 2.6-percent increase over the 12 months ending June.

evidence.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System — Chairman Kevin Warsh
evidence.excerpt: And while this summer's PCE and CPI readings were better than expected, they do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved. Here is my standard: We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do.

The number of job openings was little changed at 7.3 million in July, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. Hires and total separations both changed little at 5.1 million. Within separations, quits (3.1 million) and layoffs and discharges (1.7 million) were little changed.
